per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover Personal Care Services for beneficiaries who live in an assisted living facility?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes — NC Medicaid does cover Personal Care Services (PCS) for some beneficiaries who live in an assisted living-type setting, but only if they meet the congregate-setting eligibility criteria.

Under NC Medicaid’s congregate PCS policy, coverage applies when the beneficiary lives in a qualifying congregate facility, including an Adult Care Home licensed by North Carolina or certain licensed group homes, and also meets the required functional and medical criteria. Those criteria include needing help with qualifying activities of daily living, having PCS needs directly linked to a documented medical, mental, physical, or cognitive condition, having no other payer responsible for the service, and being medically stable without a need for continuous licensed nursing care. See § 3.2.1 of [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment).

If those criteria are met, Medicaid covers PCS in the congregate setting, including hands-on help with qualifying ADLs, related cueing or prompting, certain home-management IADLs tied to the beneficiary’s ADLs, medication assistance linked to the condition, help with adaptive devices or durable medical equipment, and certain special assistance tasks. See § 3.3 of [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment).

But Medicaid does not cover everything associated with living in assisted living. The policy specifically excludes, among other things, skilled nursing, transportation, errands, companion sitting, ongoing supervision/monitoring, and room and board. See § 4.2.1.2 of [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment).

So the short answer is: PCS can be covered in an assisted living facility, but only for eligible beneficiaries and only for covered personal care tasks — not for room and board or general assisted living costs.
